text: Drug entry DRUG-001: metformin. Biguanide oral hypoglycemic for type 2 diabetes. Starting dose 500mg PO BID, max 2550mg/day. Monitor renal function. Contraindicated in eGFR <30. Hold 48h before iodinated contrast.

Drug entry DRUG-002: lisinopril. ACE inhibitor for hypertension and heart failure. Starting dose 5-10mg daily, max 40mg. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Contraindicated in pregnancy, bilateral renal artery stenosis, and angioedema history.

Drug entry DRUG-003: warfarin. Vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant. Dose adjusted per INR (target 2.0-3.0 for most indications). Major interactions with CYP2C9 inhibitors, vitamin K-rich foods, NSAIDs. Antidote: vitamin K, 4-factor PCC.

Drug entry DRUG-004: atorvastatin. HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor for hyperlipidemia. Dose 10-80mg daily. Monitor LFTs at baseline and as indicated. Interaction with CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole). Risk of rhabdomyolysis with gemfibrozil.

Drug entry DRUG-005: albuterol. Short-acting beta-2 agonist bronchodilator. 2 puffs Q4-6H PRN for acute bronchospasm. Nebulized: 2.5mg Q4-6H. Side effects: tachycardia, tremor, hypokalemia. No dose limit in acute severe asthma.

Drug entry DRUG-006: furosemide. Loop diuretic for edema and heart failure. IV: 20-80mg, PO: 20-80mg daily. Monitor electrolytes (K, Mg, Na), renal function, volume status. Ototoxicity risk with rapid IV push or aminoglycoside combination.

Drug entry DRUG-007: amoxicillin. Aminopenicillin antibiotic. Dose 500mg-1g PO TID or 875mg BID. Covers Streptococcus, H. influenzae, E. coli. Cross-allergenicity with cephalosporins (~1-2%). Rash common with EBV infection.

Drug entry DRUG-008: omeprazole. Proton pump inhibitor for GERD and peptic ulcer. 20-40mg daily before breakfast. Long-term risks: C. difficile, hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency, bone fractures. Interaction with clopidogrel (CYP2C19).

Drug entry DRUG-009: insulin glargine. Long-acting basal insulin analog. Once daily SC injection, dose titrated to fasting glucose target. Hypoglycemia risk especially with sulfonylureas. Do not mix with other insulins. Rotate injection sites.

Drug entry DRUG-010: clopidogrel. P2Y12 antiplatelet agent. Loading dose 300-600mg, maintenance 75mg daily. Used post-ACS and post-PCI. CYP2C19 poor metabolizers have reduced efficacy. Interaction with omeprazole. Hold 5 days pre-surgery.

Drug entry DRUG-011: amlodipine. Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. 5-10mg daily for hypertension and angina. Peripheral edema most common side effect. No significant heart rate effect. Safe in asthma (unlike beta-blockers).

Drug entry DRUG-012: sertraline. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. 50-200mg daily for depression and anxiety. Black box warning for suicidality in <25 years. Serotonin syndrome risk with MAOIs, tramadol. GI side effects common initially.

Drug entry DRUG-013: prednisone. Systemic corticosteroid. Dose varies by indication (5-60mg daily). Taper required if >7 days. Side effects: hyperglycemia, immunosuppression, osteoporosis, adrenal suppression, insomnia. Monitor blood glucose in diabetics.

Drug entry DRUG-014: hydrochlorothiazide. Thiazide diuretic for hypertension. 12.5-25mg daily. Monitor electrolytes and uric acid. Hyponatremia risk in elderly. Photosensitivity. Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR <30).

Drug entry DRUG-015: gabapentin. Anticonvulsant and neuropathic pain agent. 300-1200mg TID. Dose adjust for renal impairment. Side effects: sedation, dizziness, peripheral edema. No significant drug interactions. Taper to discontinue.

Drug entry DRUG-016: metoprolol. Beta-1 selective blocker. Tartrate 25-100mg BID or succinate 25-200mg daily. Used for HTN, HF, post-MI, rate control. Contraindicated in severe bradycardia, decompensated HF, asthma. Taper to discontinue.

Drug entry DRUG-017: levothyroxine. Synthetic thyroid hormone replacement. Dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day, titrate per TSH. Take 30-60min before breakfast. Interactions with calcium, iron, PPIs (separate by 4 hours). Narrow therapeutic index.

Drug entry DRUG-018: pantoprazole. Proton pump inhibitor. 40mg IV or PO daily. Preferred over omeprazole when taking clopidogrel (less CYP2C19 interaction). Same long-term risks as other PPIs. IV formulation for NPO patients.

Drug entry DRUG-019: enoxaparin. Low molecular weight heparin. Prophylactic: 40mg SC daily. Therapeutic: 1mg/kg SC Q12H. Adjust for CrCl <30 (reduce to Q24H). Anti-Xa monitoring in obesity and renal impairment. Antidote: protamine (partial).

Drug entry DRUG-020: acetaminophen. Analgesic and antipyretic. 500-1000mg PO Q6H PRN, max 4g/day (2g/day if liver disease). Hepatotoxicity above max dose. Antidote: N-acetylcysteine. IV formulation available (1g Q6H, weight-based <50kg).

Drug entry DRUG-021: aspirin. NSAID/antiplatelet. Low-dose 81mg daily for cardiovascular prevention. Analgesic dose 325-650mg Q4-6H. GI bleeding risk, especially with anticoagulants. Contraindicated in children (Reye syndrome). Irreversible platelet inhibition.

Drug entry DRUG-022: piperacillin-tazobactam. Extended-spectrum penicillin/beta-lactamase inhibitor. 4.5g IV Q6H (3.375g if CrCl <40). Broad-spectrum coverage including Pseudomonas. Monitor renal function. Seizure risk at high doses.

Drug entry DRUG-023: vancomycin. Glycopeptide antibiotic for MRSA and C. difficile. IV: 15-20mg/kg Q8-12H, trough target 15-20 mcg/mL. PO for C. difficile only (not absorbed). Red man syndrome with rapid infusion. Nephrotoxicity monitoring.

Drug entry DRUG-024: norepinephrine. First-line vasopressor for septic shock. Start 0.1-0.5 mcg/kg/min IV, titrate to MAP >65. Central line preferred. Extravasation causes tissue necrosis (treat with phentolamine). Monitor for arrhythmia.

Drug entry DRUG-025: morphine. Opioid analgesic. IV: 2-4mg Q2-4H PRN. PO: 15-30mg Q4H. Respiratory depression risk. Histamine release causes hypotension. Renal metabolite (M6G) accumulates in renal failure. Naloxone reversal agent.

Drug entry DRUG-026: epinephrine. Catecholamine for anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest. Anaphylaxis: 0.3mg IM (autoinjector). Cardiac arrest: 1mg IV Q3-5min. Also used as vasopressor infusion. Store protected from light.

Drug entry DRUG-027: lorazepam. Benzodiazepine for anxiety, seizures, and procedural sedation. IV: 0.5-2mg Q6H PRN. Status epilepticus: 4mg IV over 2 min. Contains propylene glycol (toxicity risk with prolonged infusion). Flumazenil reversal.

Drug entry DRUG-028: ondansetron. 5-HT3 receptor antagonist antiemetic. 4mg IV/PO Q6-8H PRN. QT prolongation risk (avoid in long QT, use with caution with other QT-prolonging drugs). Constipation common. Max 16mg IV/day.

Drug entry DRUG-029: empagliflozin. SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes and heart failure. 10-25mg daily. Cardiovascular and renal benefits independent of glucose lowering. Risk of euglycemic DKA, genital mycotic infections, Fournier gangrene.

Drug entry DRUG-030: amiodarone. Class III antiarrhythmic. Loading: 150mg IV over 10min, then 1mg/min x6h, then 0.5mg/min. PO: 400mg BID x1-2 weeks then 200mg daily. Pulmonary toxicity, thyroid dysfunction, hepatotoxicity. Long half-life (40-55 days).
